args: The furin cleavage site in SARS\-CoV\-2 has no close analogue in the sampled sarbecovirus record\.
\n\nSettles on an identified natural progenitor carrying the motif, or on documentary evidence of insertion. Neither exists, which is why this one is expected to close unanswered.\n\n
SARS\-CoV\-2 was released deliberately as a Chinese state bioweapon\.

Settles on evidence of deliberate release as a weapon. The published case rests on the Yan Li-Meng reports; no review has sustained them.

Asks ONLY about deliberate release. Whether the virus was engineered is a different claim and is docketed separately in this folder, some of it running the other way — a NO here rejects the weapon story, not the laboratory one.

Filed because it is one of the most circulated claims about this pandemic, and a docket that will not hear the popular claim is not a court.
Every published version of the bioweapon claim traces to the Yan Li\-Meng preprints, which no peer review has sustained\.

Settles on the citation record: every published version of the bioweapon claim traces to the two Zenodo preprints, and on whether any peer-reviewed venue has sustained them.

Filed against the claim above rather than in place of it.
US federal grants funded coronavirus research at the Wuhan Institute of Virology\.
\n\nSettles on the grant record: the subawards from EcoHealth Alliance to the Wuhan Institute of Virology, and the NIH acknowledgements of them.\n\n
Vaccination in the first or second trimester was followed by miscarriage in 82% of completed pregnancies\.

Settles on the arithmetic in the source table: the 82% comes from dividing the losses by only those pregnancies that had already ended, when most women vaccinated early were still pregnant at the cutoff.

One of the most-repeated numbers of the pandemic, and one of the easiest to check. That is why it is here: a court that cannot settle a false number this plain cannot settle anything.
The 82% figure divides completed\-pregnancy losses by a denominator that excludes pregnancies still ongoing\.
\n\nSettles on the published table: 104 losses against a denominator of 127 counts only those vaccinated in the first or second trimester, most of whom had not finished their pregnancies.\n\n
The organiser of the February 2020 Lancet statement concealed his institute's funding relationship with the Wuhan Institute of Virology\.
\n\nSettles on the statement's own published correction and the signatory record.\n\n
mRNA COVID\-19 vaccination before 20 weeks of pregnancy raises the risk of miscarriage above the 10\-20% population baseline\.

\n\nSettles on cohort data against a population baseline. The final CDC analysis reports 10.79% across 12,097 vaccinated pregnancies, with no elevated risk week by week to twenty weeks; baseline is roughly 10 to 20%.\n\n
The 2018 DEFUSE proposal describes inserting a furin cleavage site into a SARS\-related bat coronavirus\.

Settles on the document. DRASTIC published the 2018 DARPA proposal in September 2021; the text either describes the insertion or it does not.

Asks ONLY what the proposal says. Whether the work was carried out is a different claim, and DARPA did not fund this one.
Ralph Baric's laboratory constructed the virus that became SARS\-CoV\-2\.
\n\nSettles on documentary or sequence evidence tying a construct made at that laboratory to SARS-CoV-2. Raised as a question by Sachs and others; nobody has evidenced it.\n\n
The Proximal Origin authors privately assessed the genome as showing engineered features in the week they drafted the paper rejecting that\.

Settles on the released correspondence, which is public and unredacted.

The best-evidenced claim in this folder, and the one the corpus most often garbles into something larger.
A laboratory\-associated origin is the more likely explanation, on the evidence public in 2023\.

Settles on a finding by a body with subpoena power, or a published determination the relevant experts do not contest.

Deliberately asks about the balance of evidence PUBLIC IN 2023, not the eventual truth: a claim whose answer depends on documents nobody has is unanswerable, and this docket already carries two that died that way.
Ralph Baric was excluded from the Proximal Origin author list on the ground that he was too close to the Wuhan Institute of Virology\.

Settles on the authors' own testimony to congressional investigators, which is on the record.

Filed because it cuts against the claim above from the same body of evidence that is usually cited FOR it: the party closest to the construction work was kept off the paper, deliberately, and said so.

\n\nSettles on documentary or sequence evidence tying a construct made at that laboratory to SARS-CoV-2. Raised as a question by Sachs and others; nobody has evidenced it.\n\n

Settles on the released correspondence, which is public and unredacted.

Settles on a finding by a body with subpoena power, or a published determination the relevant experts do not contest.

Deliberately asks about the balance of evidence PUBLIC IN 2023, not the eventual truth: a claim whose answer depends on documents nobody has is unanswerable, and this docket already carries two that died that way.

Settles on the authors' own testimony to congressional investigators, which is on the record.

Filed because it cuts against the claim above from the same body of evidence that is usually cited FOR it: the party closest to the construction work was kept off the paper, deliberately, and said so.
In January 2021 the director of NIAID privately raised first\-trimester miscarriage as a theoretical risk of the second vaccine dose\.

Settles on the message itself, released 10 August 2026 from a government device produced to a Senate subcommittee.

Asks only whether the message says what it is quoted as saying. What follows from it is the two claims after this one.
The January 2021 miscarriage concern was withheld from the public while the same officials recommended vaccination in pregnancy\.

Settles on comparing the private chain with the public statements over the same period.

The same message chain, one day later, weighs risks against benefits and records ten thousand vaccinated pregnancies with no signal — so the private position and the public one have to be compared whole, not by their first line.
The NIAID\-funded work at the Wuhan Institute of Virology met the federal P3CO definition of gain\-of\-function research\.

Settles on a determination by HHS or another authorised body that the funded work did or did not meet the P3CO definition.

The sharpest claim in this folder, because it is the one thing everybody is actually arguing about: nobody disputes that the money reached the work. NIH conceded in 2021 that a limited experiment met some criteria while rejecting the label.
The Proximal Origin paper was drafted at the prompting of the director of NIAID\.

\n\nSettles on the correspondence together with sworn testimony from the participants. The 1 February 2020 teleconference and the drafting timeline are documented; whether they amount to prompting is what is contested.\n\n
Testimony given to Congress in 2024 denying participation in intelligence discussions about Wuhan research was false\.
\n\nSettles on a perjury referral producing a finding, or an authoritative determination by a body with subpoena power. An accusation attached to a document release is not a finding.\n\n
The same message chain records, one day later, more than ten thousand vaccinated pregnancies with no adverse signal\.

Settles on the same released chain that carries the quoted line.

Filed because a quotation with its reply removed is a different claim from the quotation, and the docket should hold both.
